### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f313621e444d04936cb5bdaa6bc8e80e9e14dc3b` — the merge of head `324800fc44c4657c691bb5b8862df84a97cbe4af` into base `c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f313621e444d04936cb5bdaa6bc8e80e9e14dc3b && git checkout f313621e444d04936cb5bdaa6bc8e80e9e14dc3b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1 324800fc44c4657c691bb5b8862df84a97cbe4af && git checkout -B drift-repro c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1 && git merge --no-ff 324800fc44c4657c691bb5b8862df84a97cbe4af

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T17:49Z

Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34934, the P0 fix for main being red on the slow-tier scratch scan (os-dev report 6956171221).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Fixes #34934`, base `main`. Four paths, +31/-11: `skill-evals/arms.ts`, `skill-evals/self-test.ts`, `test/skill-evals/skill-evals.test.ts` and one changeset. Not governed. `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`.

**The fix.**
- `prepareArmWorkdir` drops its defaulted `base` parameter. The root is now `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'skill-eval-'))`, spelled at the call. That is the shape the scan already reads elsewhere in the same package (`skill-evals/cli.ts:134`, `join(tmpdir(), 'skill-evals-pack-')`).
- **Callers on this head.** `git grep 'prepareArmWorkdir('` finds four:
  - `run.ts:483`, the production caller, never passed a base, so a round behaves exactly as before;
  - the two `self-test.ts` rows, which stop passing `scratch` (`scratch` is still used there for `fixtureRoot` and its own cleanup, so nothing is left unused);
  - the one vitest case.
- **The test.** It now creates both roots, asserts `w.root` starts with `join(tmpdir(), 'skill-eval-')`, and removes both in a `finally`. Before, they were left to the scratch `afterAll`, and now they live outside it. The other assertions are unchanged.
- The scan and its self-test are untouched.

**Before and after.** The failing case is slow tier, which the PR's own `pull_request` and `merge_group` checks do not run, so the report's direct reading is the evidence: `unresolvedMkdtemp=1` at `arms.ts:83` at `189358f2`, then `0` at this head, and `check-dispatch-gates.mjs --slow` passes all 2564 cases. I did not re-run the slow tier. The code change is the minimal one that matches a shape the scan already resolves, so I accept the reading.

**Changeset.** `@objectstack/scenarios` patch. Note: on this head `skill-evals` runs through `tsx src/skill-evals/cli.ts` (the `package.json` script) and has no tsup entry, so I doubt the body's "arms.ts and self-test.ts ship in dist". A patch changeset is harmless either way, and `Check Changeset` is green.

**Check-runs at 8f7facaa, read at about 17:50Z.** 46 runs, none failed. Already `success`: `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Still `in_progress`: the Test Core shards, the remaining Lint legs and the remaining `Type Check ·` legs. This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. Once this lands, the first green slow-tier run on `main` (push or schedule) is the proof that #34934 is closed. Link it on the card.
- N2. The dist claim in the body: see Changeset above. Not owed.

Next: o3-F lands as soon as the three aggregates are green. No seat L2 is owed. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
